title: Emit audit log events for data residency allow/deny decisions + exporter field mapping
creator: Marcus Lin
description:
Goal
- Produce compliance-grade audit events for residency enforcement decisions (allow + deny), with a stable schema suitable for SIEM export and GRC evidence.
- Ensure events emitted from enforcement points (initially API gateway) and included in the audit-log-exporter allowlist/filters.

Background
Data residency enforcement must provide evidence that:
1) requests are evaluated against a configured policy (pinned_region / allowed_regions)
2) denies are deterministic and explainable
3) any exception / override is explicitly recorded

Scope (this ticket)
- Add audit event types and payload schema:
  - residency.policy_evaluated (emitted for every request evaluated when residency enforcement is enabled for the org/project)
  - residency.violation (emitted when a request is denied due to residency)
- Plumb required context fields from gateway enforcement middleware into the audit log event emitter.
- Update audit log exporter mappings (Splunk/Sentinel) to include new event types + required fields.
- Align fields/terminology with Security/GRC evidence requirements (Olga P.) and ensure no prompt/completion content is present.

Non-goals
- Backfill historical request decisions.
- Console UX (handled elsewhere).
- Full downstream-write enforcement events (storage writes) beyond the initial enforcement point; separate follow-up if needed.

Event definitions
1) residency.policy_evaluated
- When: after policy evaluation at enforcement point, before model execution is attempted.
- Emitted for: orgs/projects with residency enforcement enabled (feature flag + policy present). For orgs without residency enabled, do not emit (avoid cost/volume + avoids implying guarantees).
- Purpose: evidence that residency checks are being performed, with sufficient context to reproduce the decision.

2) residency.violation
- When: decision=deny and request is rejected.
- Emitted for: always when deny happens.
- Purpose: compliance evidence + customer troubleshooting.

Required fields (both events)
- event_name: "residency.policy_evaluated" | "residency.violation"
- event_version: "1"
- emitted_at: RFC3339 timestamp (UTC)
- org_id, project_id, workspace_id (where available)
- actor_type: "api_key" | "oauth" | "session" | "service"
- actor_id: stable ID (e.g., api_key_id) (no raw API key)
- request_id: Redwood request id
- trace_id: if available
- enforcement_point: "api_gateway" (initial)
- routing_mode: "hosted" | "dedicated" | "private" (best-effort from request context)
- request_region: region the request was admitted in / endpoint region (e.g., "us-east", "eu-west")
- target_region: region that would be used for execution after routing constraints (when known at enforcement time)
- policy_source: "org" | "project" | "workspace" (highest-precedence match)
- pinned_region: string or "" when unset
- allowed_regions: comma-delimited string (sorted) or "" when unset
- allow_cross_region_fallback: "true" | "false" (effective)
- decision: "allow" | "deny"
- decision_reason_code: machine-readable reason (see below)
- decision_reason: human-readable short message (single sentence)
- sdk_region_hint: region hint provided by SDK/client config if present else ""

Decision reason codes (initial)
- RESIDENCY_ALLOWED: request region satisfies policy
- RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH: request_region not in allowed_regions and/or != pinned_region
- RESIDENCY_POLICY_NOT_FOUND: enforcement enabled but no applicable policy resolved (treated as deny; indicates misconfig)
- RESIDENCY_POLICY_INVALID: policy resolved but failed validation (treated as deny)
- RESIDENCY_OVERRIDE_CROSS_REGION_FALLBACK: allowed due to explicit override (should still be auditable)

PII / content rules
- Do NOT include prompt text, completion text, embeddings payloads, uploaded files, customer-provided metadata fields, or raw IP addresses.
- user_agent: omit for now (too high entropy; can become quasi-identifier). If needed later, add as coarse bucketed value.
- client_ip: omit (future: hashed with per-tenant salt if Security wants it).

Example payloads (for docs + validation)
Event: residency.policy_evaluated (allow)
{
  "event_name": "residency.policy_evaluated",
  "event_version": "1",
  "emitted_at": "2025-02-18T17:12:43.291Z",
  "org_id": "org_4m2...",
  "project_id": "prj_c91...",
  "workspace_id": "ws_8ab...",
  "actor_type": "api_key",
  "actor_id": "key_71f...",
  "request_id": "req_01H...",
  "trace_id": "4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736",
  "enforcement_point": "api_gateway",
  "routing_mode": "hosted",
  "request_region": "eu-west",
  "target_region": "eu-west",
  "policy_source": "org",

  "allowed_regions": "eu-west",
  "allow_cross_region_fallback": "false",
  "decision": "allow",

  "decision_reason": "Request evaluated and allowed under residency policy.",

}

{
  "event_name": "residency.violation",
  "event_version": "1",
  "emitted_at": "2025-02-18T17:14:01.904Z",
  "org_id": "org_4m2...",
  "project_id": "prj_c91...",
  "workspace_id": "ws_8ab...",
  "actor_type": "api_key",
  "actor_id": "key_71f...",
  "request_id": "req_01H...",
  "trace_id": "b3b1c2d3e4f5...",
  "enforcement_point": "api_gateway",
  "routing_mode": "hosted",
  "request_region": "us-east",
  "target_region": "eu-west",
  "policy_source": "org",
  "pinned_region": "eu-west",
  "allowed_regions": "eu-west",
  "allow_cross_region_fallback": "false",
  "decision": "deny",
  "decision_reason_code": "RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH",
  "decision_reason": "Request was rejected because the endpoint region is not permitted by the residency policy.",
  "sdk_region_hint": ""
}

Implementation notes
- Emission location: gateway middleware after policy evaluation result is produced (ties to ENG-2842).
- Ensure request_id is generated before evaluation so denies also have request_id.
- Ensure org_id/project_id resolution occurs prior to emission; if only org_id is available, still emit with empty strings for missing identifiers.
- Emission path must be non-blocking for the request path; however, violations must be durably recorded. Current approach: enqueue to audit-log pipeline (Kafka) with bounded retries; if enqueue fails, increment a dedicated counter and emit a local structured log line (SRE + Security signoff).

Exporter updates
- audit-log-exporter: add event_name filters to include both residency.* events.
- Map allowed_regions as a single string field to match existing exporter constraints.
- Confirm Splunk/Sentinel examples are updated in exporter docs (PR includes sample payloads).

Acceptance criteria
- [x] New event types exist in audit schema registry with event_version=1.
- [x] For a pinned EU org hitting a US endpoint: request denied; both residency.policy_evaluated(decision=deny) and residency.violation emitted.
- [x] For an allowed request under pinned policy: residency.policy_evaluated(decision=allow) emitted.
- [x] No prompt/completion/embedding content appears in emitted audit payload.
- [x] audit-log-exporter exports these events and fields end-to-end to SIEM destination in staging.
- [x] Security/GRC signoff from Marcus L. + Olga P. that fields are sufficient for evidence.

Follow-ups
- Consider adding downstream-write enforcement audit events once ENG-28531 lands broadly (separate ticket).
- Add a minimal runbook snippet for Support to query residency.violation by org_id + time window (handled by runbook ticket).

comments: 2025-01-14 (Nadia Rahman): Drafted initial schema proposal for residency.policy_evaluated + residency.violation. Keeping content/PII out; focusing on reproducibility + evidence fields. Sending to Olga for evidence review.

2025-01-16 (Olga Petrov): Evidence needs: must include org_id, decision, request_region, effective policy (pinned/allowed), and an immutable request identifier. Prefer event emitted at admission point before execution. Also need a way to prove denies were not sampled/dropped.
2025-01-17 (Marcus Lin): +1. Ensure we can differentiate explicit override vs normal allow (decision_reason_code). Also verify actor_id is stable and doesn’t leak secrets.
2025-01-22 (Nadia Rahman): Implemented event emitter wiring behind feature flag residency_audit_events. Adds enforcement_point=api_gateway and includes sdk_region_hint when present. PR up: pr_18466.

2025-01-24 (Kevin Osei): Exporter needs allowlist updates; current exporter drops unknown event_name. I’ll handle exporter PR; please confirm final field names and whether allowed_regions should be array vs string (exporter prefers flat string).

2025-01-28 (Nadia Rahman): Adjusted allowed_regions to comma-delimited sorted string. Added policy_source and allow_cross_region_fallback effective value. Updated examples in PR description. Requested Security review.

2025-02-03 (Allison Grant): Please add a counter for audit enqueue failures and a structured log fallback; we need to alert if audit pipeline is unhealthy (even though this is “audit”, it’s now part of compliance).

2025-02-05 (Nadia Rahman): Added audit enqueue failure metric and structured fallback log line (no payload contents) with request_id + org_id + event_name + error. SRE ok with approach pending alert rule in ENG-2845.
2025-02-10 (Kevin Osei): Exporter PR submitted (pr_141). Includes Splunk sample payload and ensures residency.* events are included in export filters.
2025-02-18 (Leila Farouk): Staging E2E: pinned EU org -> US endpoint produces deny + both audit events. Allowed request produces policy_evaluated allow. Confirmed no prompt content present.
